disclaimer: Physician CME rules summarized from state medical and osteopathic boards and the FSMB board-by-board overview (Aug 2026). Rules change and some entries are marked medium confidence — confirm with your board before renewal.

md.period: Biennial, expires Dec 31 of even-numbered years
mandatory: 2 hrs pain management and opioid use/addiction (DEA registrants, each renewal; counts toward 50; waivable until DEA registration obtained)
md.notes: 50 hrs AMA/AOA/CPME Cat 1 in the 2-yr period; 25 hrs if licensed in 1st year of cycle. Specialty board initial cert/recert during the period, AMA PRA award, or residency accepted as equivalent (12 AAC 40.210). Same board for DOs.

md.period: Annual, calendar year (Jan 1–Dec 31)
mandatory: 2 hrs Cat 1 controlled-substance prescribing/abuse/chronic pain (ACSC holders, every 2 yrs; applies even if otherwise CME-exempt)
2 hrs 'Navigating Professional Boundaries in Medicine' (PBI) (all licensees, one-time; due 12/31/2025, new licensees within 12 months)
Board-prescribed collaborative/supervisory practice CME (physicians collaborating with CRNPs/CNMs or supervising PAs)
md.notes: 25 AMA PRA Cat 1/AOA 1-A or equivalent per calendar year, no rollover. ABMS certification or MOC completion counts as equivalent only for the year completed (date-specific cert). Same board licenses DOs.

md.period: Annual, renew by last day of birth month; CME window birth month to birth month
mandatory: 1 hr prescribing opioids and benzodiazepines (all physicians, each year; counts toward 20)
3 hrs prescribing education (one-time, within first 2 yrs of licensure) — per FSMB; not found in current rule text
md.notes: At least half (10 hrs) must be Cat 1 and related to primary practice area. Attestation with random monthly audits. Same board licenses DOs.

md.period: Biennial, renew on or before licensee's birthday every other year
mandatory: 3 hrs opioid-, substance-use-disorder- or addiction-related CME (DEA registrants authorized to prescribe Schedule II, each renewal)
md.notes: Arizona Medical Board (MD). 40 hrs in the 2 calendar years before renewal; ACCME Cat 1 is one of several accepted activity types (no fixed Cat 1 minimum). No carryover.

do.period: Biennial, renew by Dec 31 in alternating years (current cycle 12/31/2026); late through Apr 30, expires May 1
mandatory: 3 hrs opioid-/substance-use-disorder-/addiction-related CME (each renewal; board says applies even without DEA registration)
do.notes: Separate Board of Osteopathic Examiners. ≥24 hrs AOA Cat 1-A; ≤16 hrs AMA Cat 1. First renewal: 20 hrs (12 AOA 1-A). Postgraduate training substitutes.

md.period: Biennial, expires last day of birth month
mandatory: 12 hrs pain management & care of terminally ill/dying incl. Schedule II addiction risk (one-time, by 2nd renewal; or 12-hr opiate-dependent/buprenorphine course by next renewal; pathology/radiology exempt)
20% of CME in geriatrics (general internists/family physicians with >25% patients aged 65+, each renewal)
md.notes: Medical Board of California. AMA PRA Cat 1 (or AAFP prescribed/board-accepted). Passing a specialty board cert/recert exam = 100 hrs credit for 4 yrs. CME courses must include implicit-bias content (course rule).

do.period: Biennial; CME period matches the 2-yr renewal period (since 1/1/2022)
mandatory: 1 hr addiction to Schedule II drugs/opioids (each renewal)
12 hrs pain management & terminally ill/dying patients (one-time, within 4 yrs of licensure or by 2nd renewal; or 12-hr opiate-dependent/buprenorphine alternative; pathology/radiology exempt)
do.notes: Separate Osteopathic Medical Board of California. ≥20 of 50 hrs AOA Cat 1-A or 1-B. CME must include implicit-bias curriculum. Geriatrics rule not stated by OMBC.

md.period: Biennial, expires Apr 30 of odd-numbered years (first CME-audited renewal: 2027)
mandatory: 2 hrs opioid/benzodiazepine prescribing, SUD recognition/referral & PDMP use (each renewal; exempt if national board cert requires equivalent training or attest no opioid prescribing)
md.notes: New under HB24-1153. Accepts AMA PRA Cat 1, AAFP prescribed, AOA 1-A, and qualifying national board certification activities. Prorated for new licensees; up to 5% audited.

md.period: Annual renewal (birth month); 50 contact hrs in the preceding 24 months
mandatory: 1 hr infectious diseases incl. HIV/AIDS (first renewal requiring CME, then every 6 yrs)
1 hr risk management incl. controlled-substance prescribing & pain management (first CME renewal, then every 6 yrs)
2 hrs behavioral health incl. suicide prevention/veterans' mental health (first CME renewal, then every 6 yrs)
1 hr each sexual assault, domestic violence, cultural competency (listed on DPH page; FSMB says optional within risk mgmt since 10/2022)
md.notes: Contact hour = 50 min; activities from AMA/AOA/CSMS/hospital/etc. accepted, no Cat 1 minimum. First renewal exempt. Up to 10 hrs waivable for board service. Keep records 6 yrs.

md.period: Biennial; DC Health moving all licenses to expire last day of birth month (odd/even year by birth year); 2026 renewal deadline was Jun 30, 2026
mandatory: 2 hrs LGBTQ cultural competency (each renewal)
5 hrs (≥10%) DC Health public-health-priority topics, e.g. opioid prescribing, abuse/trafficking/DV, implicit bias (each renewal)
At least 1 course in pharmacology (each renewal)
md.notes: Board of Medicine; 50 AMA PRA Cat 1 hrs in the 2 yrs before expiration (17 DCMR 4615). One-time 50% CE relief for licensees with <2-yr term; LGBTQ and public-health hours still required.

md.period: Biennial, Apr 1–Mar 31; expires Mar 31 of odd-numbered years
mandatory: 2 hrs controlled-substance prescribing/chronic pain (Delaware CSR holders, each 2-yr CSR renewal)
md.notes: AMA Cat I or AOA equivalent. 20 hrs if licensed >1 but <2 yrs at first renewal; none if <1 yr. CSR applicants also take a 1-hr two-part course (not CE credit).

md.period: Biennial, expires Jan 31 (Group 1 even years, Group 2 odd years)
mandatory: 2 hrs prevention of medical errors (each renewal)
2 hrs controlled-substance prescribing (DEA registrants, each renewal; must cover sickle cell pain treatment from 7/1/2026)
2 hrs domestic violence (every third biennium; within the 38)
1 hr HIV/AIDS (one-time, before first renewal)
md.notes: Board of Medicine: 38 hrs AMA Cat I (or ACEP/AAFP/ACOG equivalents) + 2 hrs medical errors. No carryover. Volunteer service can waive up to 25% of non-mandatory hours.

do.period: Biennial, expires Mar 31 of even-numbered years
mandatory: 1 hr Florida laws & rules / professional and medical ethics (each renewal)
2 hrs prevention of medical errors (each renewal)
2 hrs controlled-substance prescribing (DEA registrants, each renewal; must cover sickle cell pain treatment from 7/1/2026)
1 hr HIV/AIDS (one-time, before first renewal)
2 hrs domestic violence (every third biennium)
do.notes: Separate Board of Osteopathic Medicine. ≥20 hrs AOA Cat 1-A (required courses may count if 1-A). Home study ≤8 hrs. Partial-cycle renewal: 6 hrs.

md.period: Biennial, expires last day of birth month
mandatory: 3 hrs AMA/AOA Cat 1 controlled-substance prescribing (DEA holders who prescribe controlled substances, one-time)
2 hrs professional boundaries & sexual misconduct (all physicians, one-time, since 1/1/2022)
20 hrs pain management/palliative medicine per biennium (only if ≥50% of patients are opioid pain patients and not pain/palliative certified)
md.notes: All hours must be AMA/AOA Cat 1 or listed equivalents (AAFP Prescribed, ACOG Cognates Cat 1, ACEP Cat 1). First renewal exempt. Up to 10 hrs waivable for free care, 8 for peer review. FSMB lists opioid hrs as each renewal; rule says one-time.

md.period: Biennial, renew by Jan 31 of even-numbered years (hours earned in the 2 preceding calendar years)
md.notes: 40 Cat 1 or 1A hrs; first renewal 20 hrs. Board cert, board exams, teaching and memberships don't count. Old HAR 16-85 text (100 hrs incl. Cat 2) superseded in practice per board audit notice.

do.period: Biennial, renew by Jun 30 of even-numbered years
do.notes: DOs licensed by the Hawaii Medical Board but on a separate June 30 cycle. Statute requires Cat 1/1A CME per board rules; 40-hr figure assumed same as MD (not confirmed on DO page).

md.period: Biennial, expires first day of birth month
mandatory: 2 hrs child abuse identification/reporting (regularly provide primary care to children, every 3 yrs)
2 hrs dependent adult abuse identification/reporting (regularly provide primary care to adults, every 3 yrs)
2 hrs Cat 1 CDC opioid prescribing guidelines (prescribed opioids in prior period, every 5 yrs)
2 hrs Cat 1 end-of-life care (regularly care for actively dying patients, every 5 yrs)
md.notes: 40 hrs Cat 1 or board-approved equivalent; up to 20 hrs carryover. ABMS/AOA certification or recertification within the license period = 50 Cat 1 hrs. Rules now 481 IAC 654 (eff. May 21, 2025).

md.period: 40 hrs per 2-year CME cycle; license renewal date not confirmed
md.notes: Per FSMB (Aug 2026): all Cat 1; ABMS/AOA/Royal College cert or recert during the cycle may replace CME. Board now under DOPL (IDAPA 22.01.01.079). Board pages could not be fetched.

md.period: Triennial, expires July 31 (2026 renewal extended to Aug 31, 2026; next July 31, 2029)
mandatory: 1 hr sexual harassment prevention (all, each renewal)
1 hr implicit bias awareness (all, each renewal)
3 hrs safe opioid prescribing (controlled substance license holders; mandated topics may be spread over 2 triennial periods per 20 ILCS 2105-375)
1 hr cultural competency (all, every 6 yrs / 2 renewals)
1 hr Alzheimer's/dementia (those treating patients 26+; before end of first renewal period, then every 6 yrs)
Mandated reporter child abuse training (DCFS; within 3 months of role, then every 6 yrs)
md.notes: Mandated hours count toward the 150. First renewal after initial licensure exempt from the 150 hrs. Up to 90 hrs may be informal (Cat 2). CME done for board certification counts.

md.period: Biennial, expires Oct 31 of odd years
mandatory: 2 hrs opioid prescribing & opioid abuse within prior 2 yrs (Indiana CSR applicants/re-registrants; SEA 225-2018)
md.notes: No general CME hour requirement for license renewal. Only CSR holders need the 2-hr opioid CE, due with CSR renewal (same Oct 31 odd-year cycle).

md.period: Annual, MD licenses expire June 30; CME counted in the 18 months before expiration
mandatory: 1 hr Category III (acute/chronic pain mgmt, opioid prescribing, or PDMP use) per annual renewal; counts within the 50
md.notes: Alternative look-backs: 100 credits/30 mo (40 Cat I, 2 Cat III) or 150/42 mo (60 Cat I, 3 Cat III). Kansas 'Category I' is board-defined, not strictly AMA PRA Cat 1. First renewal exempt.

do.period: Annual, DO licenses expire Sept 30; CME counted in the 18 months before expiration
mandatory: 1 hr Category III (pain mgmt, opioid prescribing, or PDMP use) per annual renewal
do.notes: Same Board of Healing Arts rules as MDs; only the expiration date differs.

md.period: 3-yr CME cycle, current Jan 1 2024-Dec 31 2026 (next 2027-2029); license renews annually by March 1
mandatory: 4.5 hrs KASPER/pain mgmt/addiction disorders (controlled substance prescribers/dispensers, each 3-yr cycle)
3 hrs domestic violence (primary care physicians, one-time within 3 yrs of initial licensure)
1 hr pediatric abusive head trauma (peds, radiology, FM, EM, urgent care; one-time within 5 yrs of initial licensure)
md.notes: Passing an ABMS/AOA certification or recertification exam = 60 hrs; accredited postgrad training = 50 hrs/yr. Mandated topics still required. HIV/AIDS CE no longer required (2015).

md.period: Annual, renew on or before first day of birth month
mandatory: 3 hrs CDS prescribing/drug diversion/addiction/chronic pain (CDS license holders, one-time before first renewal)
1 hr sickle cell disease + 1 hr refresher every 3 yrs (emergency medicine only)
1 hr nutrition & metabolic health every 4 yrs (listed specialties incl. FM, IM, peds, surgery, OB/GYN, etc.; from cycle beginning Jan 1, 2026)
md.notes: Exempt from annual CME if certified/recertified by an ABMS or AOA board within the past year (exemption only, not ongoing MOC). First-year licensees exempt.
sources: https://www.ag.louisiana.gov/Files/OLRP/Reviews/Louisiana State Board of Medical Examiners/2026.04.24 LSBME CME/Submission Documents/CME NOI redline.pdf

md.period: Biennial, on licensee's birthday
mandatory: 10 credits risk management (all, each renewal; up to 7 may be physician wellness)
2 credits reading Board regulations 243 CMR 1-3 (each renewal; counts toward risk mgmt)
2 credits implicit bias (each renewal since 6/1/2022; counts toward risk mgmt)
3 credits opioid education & pain management (if prescribing controlled substances, each renewal)
2 credits end-of-life care (one-time)
3 credits EHR proficiency (one-time, exemptions apply)
1 credit Alzheimer's/dementia (serving adults, one-time)
Child abuse/neglect recognition & reporting (one-time)
Domestic & sexual violence training (one-time)
md.notes: Policy 17-05 CME pilot in effect: 50 credits Cat 1 or 2 (no Cat 1 minimum; was 100 with 40 Cat 1). Mandated credits count within the 50. No carryover.

md.period: Biennial, expires Sept 30; last names A-L even years, M-Z odd years
mandatory: Implicit bias training (one-time, first renewal after Apr 1, 2022)
Structural racism training (one-time, first renewal after Apr 1, 2026)
2 hrs CDS prescribing/dispensing (CDS registrants, attest at CDS registration renewal)
md.notes: Active time-limited ABMS/AOA/RCPSC/CFPC certification with proof of maintenance dated within 5 yrs of renewal meets CME. First renewal: no CME but New Physician Orientation required.

md.period: Biennial, expires last day of birth month (even/odd year matches birth year)
mandatory: 3 hrs Cat 1 opioid prescribing (all BOLIM licensees, each 2-yr cycle; required even if using ABMS certification)
md.notes: Since Feb 3, 2026 current ABMS certification incl. MOC satisfies the 40 hrs (not lifetime certs). MD and DO boards merge into a Board of Medicine Jan 1, 2027; current rules stay until new rules.

do.period: Biennial, expires end of birth month
mandatory: 3 hrs Cat 1 opioid prescribing (opioid prescribers, each 2-yr cycle)
do.notes: Board of Osteopathic Licensure: 40% (40 hrs) must be osteopathic CME - AOA Cat 1 for primary care; specialists may use AOA, ACGME or AMA Cat 1. Merges into Board of Medicine Jan 1, 2027.

md.period: Triennial (secondary source: expires Jan 31 of renewal year; confirm on LARA)
mandatory: 1 hr medical ethics (each cycle)
3 hrs pain & symptom management (each cycle)
1 hr implicit bias per year of licensure (3 hrs per renewal; 2 hrs for initial license)
Human trafficking training (one-time)
Opioids & controlled substances awareness training (one-time, controlled substance prescribers)
md.notes: Board of Medicine (MD). Specialty certification maintenance counts for at most 30 Cat 1 hrs; not a full substitute.

do.period: Triennial (renewal date per LARA; not confirmed)
mandatory: 1 hr medical ethics (each cycle)
3 hrs pain & symptom management incl. 1 hr controlled substance prescribing (each cycle)
1 hr implicit bias per year of licensure (3 hrs per renewal)
Human trafficking training (one-time)
Opioids & controlled substances awareness training (one-time, controlled substance prescribers)
do.notes: Separate Board of Osteopathic Medicine & Surgery; 60 Cat 1 (AOA or AMA). No equivalents accepted.

md.period: License renews annually (birth-month based); CME reported per 3-yr cycle from initial licensure - not confirmed
md.notes: No mandated topics listed by FSMB (Aug 2026). Board may accept ABMS/AOA/RCPSC certification, recertification or MOC in lieu of CME (Minn. R. 5605.0700).

md.period: Biennial reporting period preceding renewal (expiration date not confirmed)
mandatory: 1 hr health benefits of nutrition (all, each biennial cycle)
md.notes: All hours AMA Cat 1 or AOA 1-A/2-A, or 40 Cat 1/1-A hrs with posttesting. Specialty board certification/recertification during the period = requirement met (20 CSR 2150-2.125).

md.period: 2-yr CME cycle (July 1-June 30); license renews annually by June 30 - not confirmed
mandatory: 5 hrs (within the 40) on prescribing medications with emphasis on controlled substances (likely DEA registrants, each cycle - applicability unconfirmed)
md.notes: Active ABMS certification with ongoing MOC can replace the Board-approved CME tracking account; lifetime certification does not qualify. AOA Cat 1-A accepted for DOs.

md.period: biennial, physician licenses renew by March 31 (ARM 24.101.413)
md.notes: No state CME requirement for MD/DO license renewal. Only the federal DEA MATE Act one-time 8 hr SUD training applies (not a state rule). Same board licenses MDs and DOs.

md.period: 60 hrs per 3-year CME cycle; license registration renews annually around the licensee's birthday
mandatory: 3 hrs controlled-substance prescribing practices, recognizing abuse/misuse and chronic pain prescribing (controlled-substance prescribers, each 3-yr cycle; counts toward 60)
md.notes: All Cat 1 and relevant to current or intended specialty (21 NCAC 32R .0101). Attesting to ABMS, AOA or RCPSC recert/MOC participation meets the full cycle requirement. Same board for DOs.

md.period: 40 hrs per 2-year CME period (N.D. Admin. Code 50-04-01-02); renewal date not confirmed
md.notes: All Cat 1. No state-mandated topics. Physicians holding current ABMS, AOA or RCPSC certification, MOC or recert at time of audit are exempt. Same board for DOs.

md.period: biennial, licenses expire Oct 1 of even-numbered years
mandatory: 3 hrs opioid prescribing incl. 0.5 hr PDMP (controlled-substance prescribers, each renewal; counts toward 50)
md.notes: ACCME/AOA Category 1. AMA PRA award or AOA CME certificate earned in prior 24 mo substitutes. Up to 25 hrs carry over. One GME year = 50 hrs. Same rules for DOs.

md.period: biennial; CME window is the 2 calendar years (Jan 1 to Dec 31) before the renewal year; renewal year depends on licensure date
mandatory: 3 hrs pain management and/or addiction disorder / opioid prescribing (NH DEA registrants, each biennial renewal; counts toward 100; RSA 126-A:97)
md.notes: Max 60 hrs Cat 2. Current MOC, or passing an ABMS specialty board exam/recert in the cycle, satisfies CME (counted as 100 Cat 1 hrs), except the DEA opioid hours. Same rules for DOs.

md.period: biennial, licenses expire June 30 of odd-numbered years (current period 7/1/2025 to 6/30/2027)
mandatory: 2 hrs Cat 1 end-of-life care (each renewal)
1 hr Cat 1 opioid prescribing / pain management / SUD (each renewal)
2 hrs Cat 1 sexual misconduct prevention incl. human trafficking identification (each renewal, from period starting 7/1/2025)
1 hr Cat 1 explicit and implicit bias (physicians providing perinatal care, each renewal)
6 hrs cultural competency (one-time; physicians licensed before 3/2/2005 or without it in med school)
md.notes: Up to 60 hrs Cat 2. Attestation with audit. New licensees who finished GME within 12 months of licensure are exempt for the first biennial period. Same board and rules for DOs.

md.period: triennial, renewal due July 1 of the renewal year; CME earned July 1 to June 30 of the 3 years before renewal
mandatory: 1 hr review of NM Medical Practice Act and board rules (each renewal; counts toward 75)
5 hrs pain management (holders of both DEA and NM controlled-substance registrations, each triennial cycle; also 5 hrs in first year of licensure)
md.notes: Accepted: AMA PRA Cat 1, AOA/CCME 1-A/1-B, plus teaching, publication, preceptor and GME credit (no Cat 2 self-study). AMA PRA award, ABMS/AOA board cert or recert in cycle, or passing SPEX/COMVEX substitute.

md.period: biennial, MD licenses expire June 30 of odd-numbered years (next 6/30/2027)
mandatory: 2 hrs ethics, pain management or addiction care (all, each renewal)
2 hrs misuse/abuse of controlled substances, opioid prescribing or addiction (registered to dispense controlled substances, each renewal)
2 hrs suicide detection/intervention/prevention (all, within 2 yrs of initial licensure then every 4 yrs)
2 hrs SBIRT (all, one-time within 2 yrs of initial licensure)
2 hrs HIV stigma/bias (MDs providing/supervising hospital emergency or primary care, within 2 yrs of starting)
2 hrs cultural competency/DEI (psychiatrists only, each renewal)
md.notes: All AMA PRA Cat 1 (or board-approved). Min 20 hrs in scope of practice/specialty. Prorated 30/20/10 hrs for first renewal by licensure date. Up to 4 hrs double credit (geriatrics, medication mgmt, rare disease).

do.period: annual, DO licenses expire Dec 31 (moving to biennial renewal after 12/31/2026 under AB 56 / proposed R092-25)
mandatory: 2 hrs misuse/abuse of controlled substances, opioid prescribing or addiction (each renewal)
2 hrs ethics, pain management or addiction care (even-numbered years)
2 hrs evidence-based suicide prevention (within 2 yrs of initial licensure then every 4 yrs)
2 hrs SBIRT (one-time, within 2 yrs of initial licensure)
2 hrs HIV stigma/bias (DOs providing/supervising hospital emergency or primary care, within 2 yrs of starting)
2 hrs cultural competency/DEI (psychiatrists only)
do.notes: Separate Board of Osteopathic Medicine. 35 hrs/yr incl. 10 AOA Cat 1-A (NAC 633.250). For renewals after 12/31/2026: 40 hrs per biennium incl. 20 Cat 1-A and 4 hrs controlled-substance topics (proposed reg R092-25).

md.period: biennial registration; due date varies by licensee (based on registration date)
mandatory: 2 hrs child abuse identification and reporting (one-time; plus a one-time updated-curriculum course due by 4/1/2025 for those trained before)
Infection control and barrier precautions (at initial licensure, then every 4 years; no fixed hours)
3 hrs pain management, palliative care and addiction (DEA-registered prescribers incl. residents using a facility DEA number, every 3 years)
md.notes: No general CME hour requirement. Only the mandated trainings listed apply. Same rules for DOs (NYSED State Board for Medicine).

md.period: biennial; expiration date varies by licensee
mandatory: 1 hr duty to report (each renewal; counts toward 50)
20 hrs Cat 1 pain medicine incl. addiction potential (pain management clinic owners/operators only, every 2 yrs; counts toward 50)
md.notes: All Category 1 (AMA PRA Cat 1 or AOA 1-A). Board certification not accepted as an equivalent (OAC 4731-10-02). State Medical Board of Ohio licenses MDs and DOs under the same rules.

md.period: 60 hrs per 3-year CME period; license renews annually (exact renewal date not confirmed)
mandatory: 1 hr pain management or opioid use/addiction (valid DEA registrants, every year before renewal)
1 hr health care providers' rights and responsibilities training (every 2 years)
md.notes: All Cat 1 (OAC 435:10-15-1). AMA PRA award or ABMS specialty certification/recertification obtained during the 3-yr period substitutes. Applies to MDs only; DOs have a separate board.

mandatory: 1 hr prescribing, dispensing and administering controlled substances (each year; exempt if no OBN and DEA registration)
do.notes: Separate State Board of Osteopathic Examiners. 16 hrs/yr, all AOA Category 1-A or 1-B (OAC 510:10-3-8). Board certification not accepted as an equivalent.

md.period: biennial (30 hrs if licensed in the 2nd year of the biennium); renewal date not confirmed
mandatory: 1 hr pain management (Pain Management Commission course; at initial licensure then every 24 months)
1 hr cultural competency (every year; residents and volunteer camp licensees excepted)
md.notes: CME must be AMA PRA Cat 1 or AOA 1-A/2-A. Ongoing ABMS or AOA-BOS recertification/MOC participation meets the requirement in place of CME (OAR 847-008-0070). Same board for DOs.

md.period: biennial, MD licenses expire Dec 31 of even-numbered years
mandatory: 12 hrs patient safety or risk management (each renewal; counts toward 100)
2 hrs child abuse recognition and reporting, DHS-approved (each renewal)
2 hrs pain management or addiction identification + 2 hrs opioid prescribing/dispensing (within 12 months of initial licensure, one-time)
2 hrs pain management, addiction identification or prescribing practices (each later renewal)
2 hrs organ and tissue donation (one-time, within 5 yrs of initial licensure or renewal, effective 5/1/2026)
md.notes: Remainder may be Cat 1 or 2 (49 Pa. Code 16.19). ABMS specialty certification is accepted as documentation of Category 1 credit, not as a full CME substitute. Applies to MDs only.

do.period: biennial, DO licenses expire Oct 31 of even-numbered years
mandatory: 12 hrs patient safety or risk management, Cat 1 or 2 (each renewal)
2 hrs child abuse recognition and reporting, DHS-approved (each renewal)
2 hrs pain management or addiction identification + 2 hrs opioid prescribing/dispensing (within 12 months of initial licensure, one-time)
2 hrs pain management, addiction identification or prescribing practices (each later renewal)
2 hrs organ and tissue donation (one-time, within 5 yrs of initial licensure or renewal, effective 5/1/2026)
do.notes: Separate State Board of Osteopathic Medicine (49 Pa. Code 25.271). The 20 Category 1 hrs must be AOA Cat 1-A; remainder Cat 1 or 2. Board certification not accepted as an equivalent.

md.period: Biennial; license expires July 1 of even years; CME must be earned by June 1 of even years
mandatory: 1 hr cognitive impairment/Alzheimer's & dementia (one-time, all physicians, since Aug 1 2019)
8 hrs Cat 1 opioid/pain prescribing (one-time, Schedule II opioid prescribers, before CSR renewal)
md.notes: All 40 hrs AMA PRA Cat 1 or AOA 1-A. ABMS MOC or AOA OCC participation deemed equivalent. One 6-month extension possible. Same board licenses DOs.

md.period: Biennial; expires June 30 of odd years
mandatory: 2 hrs prescribing & monitoring controlled substances (within the 40, each renewal, CME pathway)
1 hr human trafficking (EM, primary care, IM, FM, peds, OB/GYN, hospitalists only; by Jan 1 2028 if licensed before 2026, then every 6 yrs)
md.notes: All AMA/AOA Cat 1; at least 30 hrs related to practice area. Alternatives: specialty board recertification/added qualifications, ACGME/AOA training, SPEX/COMVEX. Same board licenses DOs.

md.period: Biennial renewal fee (SDCL 36-4-24.1); expiration date set per license, online renewal opens 90 days prior
md.notes: No state CME requirement for MD/DO license renewal. Single board (Medical and Osteopathic Examiners) for MDs and DOs.

md.period: Biennial; expires end of birth month, even/odd year by birth year; CME counted over the 24-month renewal cycle
mandatory: 2 hrs controlled-substance prescribing incl. TN chronic pain guidelines (within the 40, each renewal; certain pain-specialty exemptions)
md.notes: AMA PRA Cat 1 (or AAFP/AOA prescribed). Up to 10 hrs for case review for the Dept. Separate CE applies to 'identified high prescribers'. Exempt the year USMLE Step 3 is passed.

do.period: Biennial; 24 months ending on license expiration date
mandatory: 2 hrs controlled-substance prescribing incl. TN treatment guidelines (within the 40, each renewal)
do.notes: Separate Board of Osteopathic Examination. Hours must be AOA 1-A, 2-A and/or 1-B (max 20 in 1-B); AOA-, ACCME- or AAFP-approved courses accepted.

md.period: Biennial; expires Feb 28, May 31, Aug 31 or Nov 30 (assigned at licensure); even-numbered licenses in even years, odd in odd
mandatory: 2 hrs medical ethics/professional responsibility (all, each renewal, formal)
1 hr HHSC-approved human trafficking (direct patient care; first renewal, then every 3rd renewal)
2 hrs opioid/pain prescribing (direct patient care; within 1 yr of licensure and 2nd renewal, then every 8 yrs)
1 hr nutrition & metabolic health (all; licenses expiring on/after May 30 2027)
2 hrs forensic evidence collection (ER/urgent care physicians; licenses expiring from Feb 28 2027)
Life of the Mother Act course (one-time; OB care and designated specialties)
md.notes: 24 formal (AMA Cat 1/AOA 1-A) + up to 24 informal. Board cert/recert within 36 mo or current MOC/OCC presumes compliance with hours (not human trafficking). CE Broker tracking from Sept 1 2026.

md.period: Biennial; expires January 31 of even years
mandatory: 3.5 hrs DOPL-approved controlled-substance prescribing (CS licensees, each renewal)
1 DOPL-listed online suicide prevention course (each renewal)
Controlled substance database tutorial & exam (CS prescribers)
md.notes: 34 of 40 must be ACCME Cat 1; up to 6 hrs may be DOPL-sponsored; up to 15% from documented volunteer care. ACGME residency counts pro rata.

do.period: Biennial; expires May 31 of even years
mandatory: 3.5 hrs DOPL-approved controlled-substance prescribing (CS licensees, each renewal)
1 DOPL-listed online suicide prevention course (each renewal)
do.notes: Separate Osteopathic Physician & Surgeon board under DOPL (R156-68-304). 34 of 40 must be AOA or ACCME Category 1.

md.period: Biennial; renew during birth month (18VAC85-20-230)
mandatory: 1 hr human trafficking (one-time; board-designated for renewal cycles beginning 2024-2025, per DHP notice 12/6/2023)
4 hrs anesthesia topics (only if administering office-based anesthesia without anesthesiologist/CRNA, each renewal)
md.notes: Cut from 60 hrs (30 Type 1) to 30 hrs all Type 1, eff. 2/27/2025; old 2-hr pain/opioid mandate no longer in rule. First renewal exempt. Board FAQ: specialty recert may count if board deems equivalent.

md.period: Biennial (expiration believed Nov 30 of even years; not confirmed on board site)
mandatory: 1 hr hospice, palliative care or pain management (all, each renewal)
2 hrs safe prescribing of controlled substances & pain management (DEA registrants, each renewal)
md.notes: Board of Medical Practice, 12-5 Vt. Code R. 200:22.1. Category requirement and exact expiration date could not be confirmed on the board site.

do.period: Biennial (Office of Professional Regulation; exact date not confirmed)
do.notes: Separate Board of Osteopathic Physicians under OPR (26 V.S.A. 1836). FSMB lists no topic mandates; VDH opioid rule may still require 2 hrs for DEA registrants (unconfirmed).

md.period: License renews annually on birthday; CME attested every 4 years
mandatory: 6 hrs suicide assessment, treatment & management (one-time, first full CME cycle)
2 hrs health equity (each 4-yr cycle)
1 hr opioid prescribing best practices/rules (one-time, opioid prescribers)
md.notes: WAC 246-919-460: Cat 1 unlimited; max 80 hrs each in Categories 2-5. Equivalents: ABMS cert within 4 yrs, current MOC, or AMA PRA award in 2 of prior 4 yrs.

do.period: License renews annually on birthday; CME attested every 3 years
mandatory: 6 hrs suicide assessment, treatment & management (one-time)
2 hrs health equity (each CME cycle)
1 hr opioid prescribing (one-time, opioid prescribers)
do.notes: Separate Board of Osteopathic Medicine and Surgery (WAC 246-853-070/-080). ABOMS or ABMS cert/recert within last 6 yrs accepted as equivalent.

md.period: Biennial; expires Oct 31 of odd years (from knowledge; not confirmed on DSPS site)
mandatory: 2 hrs opioid/controlled-substance prescribing (within the 30, each renewal; DEA registrants per secondary source)
md.notes: Wis. Admin. Code Med 13.02: all AMA/AOA Cat 1; opioid courses no longer need specific MEB approval; DEA-required courses may count. Same board for MD/DO.

md.period: Biennial, July 1-June 30 reporting period (expiration year by licensee not confirmed)
mandatory: 3 hrs board-approved drug diversion/best-practice CS prescribing (each renewal, counts within 50; CS prescribers/dispensers)
Nutrition CME (all; eff. July 1 2026 per HB 4951; hours not specified)
md.notes: All Cat 1; 30 in specialty; up to 20 hrs for teaching/precepting. ABMS cert/recert exam, MOC, or 1 yr ACGME training substitutes but not for the 3-hr prescribing course.

do.period: Biennial, July 1-June 30 reporting period (exact expiration year not confirmed)
mandatory: 3 hrs board-approved drug diversion/best-practice CS prescribing (each renewal)
Nutrition CME (all; eff. July 1 2026 per HB 4951; hours not specified)
do.notes: Separate Board of Osteopathic Medicine (W. Va. Code R. 24-1-15). 16 of 32 must be AOA 1-A or 1-B. Residency >9 months of period may substitute.

md.period: CME measured over 3-year period; license renews annually (renewal date not confirmed)
mandatory: 1 hr responsible prescribing or SUD treatment (WY controlled-substance registrants, every 2 yrs)
md.notes: Board of Medicine Rules Ch. 3 s.7: any mix of AMA Cat 1/2 or AOA CME; current AMA PRA award or current ABMS specialty certificate accepted as equivalent. Same board for MD/DO.

abo.summary: ABO Continuing Certification runs on a 10-year cycle. Requirements: valid license, CME with self-assessment (attested every 2 years), 1 patient safety activity, Quarterly Questions (5 annual passes), 2 Improvement in Medical Practice activities, and an annual fee.
annual: Annual fee $225, assessed Jan 1 each calendar year; must be paid before accessing CC activities
Quarterly Questions: 1 yearly set (40 knowledge Qs = 30 subspecialty/comprehensive + 10 core; plus 10 article-based Qs on 5 chosen articles)
Maintain a valid, unrestricted medical license (license attestation via Status Page)
Quarterly Questions year completion = 8 AMA PRA Category 1 credits with self-assessment credit (optional to claim)
cycle: 10-year cycle; certificates are time-limited (expire Dec 31 of final year (unconfirmed))
CME: average 50 AMA PRA Category 1 credits every 2 years (= 250 per 10 years), incl. 16 self-assessment credits per 2 years
At least 80% of CME must be ophthalmology-specific; must be from ACCME-accredited providers
Attest to CME on ABO site every 2 years; diplomates without attestation by Year 4 may be audited
1 patient safety activity per 10-year cycle (attest once)
Quarterly Questions: meet annual passing standard 5 times before certificate expires
Improvement in Medical Practice: 2 activities per 10-year cycle
No extensions to complete the program (policy effective Jan 1, 2024)

cmeCredits.notes: AMA PRA Category 1 only; 16 of each 50 must be self-assessment; >=80% ophthalmology-specific; plus 1 patient safety activity per cycle. Fast-Track/reinstatement: 250 Cat 1 credits within last 10 years, attested once.

quarterlyQuestions.notes: 50 total per yearly set: 40 scored knowledge Qs (30 subspecialty or comprehensive + 10 core) released in Q1-Q2, plus 10 article Qs on 5 chosen articles in Q3; Q4 is an optional bonus quarter. 60-second timer per question. Self-paced: no fixed quarterly deadline; all Qs for a year must be answered to count. Each year's set stays available 5 years (2026 set removed after 12/31/2030). Pass = >= annual standard (65% for 2022-2026) on knowledge Qs + complete article section. Need 5 passes per 10-year cycle; answered Qs cannot be retaken. Accessed at questions.abop.org.

practiceImprovement.notes: Improvement in Medical Practice: 2 activities per 10-year cycle, chosen from ABO menu and attested on Status Page. Options include ABO/AAO/OMIC webinars, QQ improvement articles, designated AAO courses, Stanford unconscious bias course, root cause analysis, PPP-based or self-directed improvement projects, ABMS Portfolio Program, Clarkson Award. Patient safety (separate, 1 per cycle) can be met via QQ patient-safety articles (3), QQ controlled-substance articles (5, from 2025), ABMS directory course, OMIC module, or DEA 8-hour MATE training.

reporting.notes: CME is attested by the diplomate on the ABO Status Page; not automatically reported. AAO members can transfer an AAO CME transcript to ABO by entering ABO ID on the Academy transcript page (still must attest). ABMS-directory activity completions are not auto-transferred. ABO offers an optional CME tracker. Public verification shows primary status (Certified / Not Certified / Retired / Board Eligible), detail (time-limited, recertified, Clinically Inactive, On Probation), certification date ranges, and a 'Participating in Continuing Certification' badge. No ABO-PARS/CME Passport auto-feed confirmed (unconfirmed).

recentChanges: Jan 1, 2024: no extensions granted to complete Continuing Certification
2025: QQ controlled-substance article set added as a patient safety option
DOCK exam retired; all diplomates now on Quarterly Questions

aoboo.summary: Osteopathic ophthalmologists certify through the AOA's combined American Osteopathic Boards of Ophthalmology and Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (AOBOO-HNS). OCC has 4 components: active licensure, CME, cognitive assessment (annual longitudinal assessment), and practice improvement.
annual: Longitudinal assessment: 30 questions per calendar year, open mid-January to Oct 31; pass >= 70%
LA registration fee $200/yr (+$50 late fee); register in prior year (2026 registration ran Jun 1-Oct 31, 2025)
cycle: CME (Component 2), 2025-2027 cycle: 60 total credits over 3 years incl. 25 ophthalmology-specific (time-limited or OCC-participating)
Non-time-limited, not in OCC: 120 credits over 3 years incl. 25 specialty-specific
Practice improvement (Component 4): QI activity attestation every 3 years via AOA Physician Portal
OCC cycle referenced as 10 years (unconfirmed for ophthalmology certificate length)

cmeCredits.notes: 25 must be specialty-specific; Category 1 (osteopathic) minimum for AOBOO not stated in AOA table (unconfirmed). 120 if non-time-limited and not in OCC.

quarterlyQuestions.notes: Not quarterly: one annual longitudinal assessment of 30 questions, mid-Jan to Oct 31. Remediation/second attempt opens 7 days after first. Failure: 6 months next year to retake; failing retake may make certification inactive. From Jan 26, 2026 delivered in AOA Learning Portal (powered by Oasis).

practiceImprovement.notes: Component 4: complete required Quality Improvement activity attestations every 3 years via AOA Physician Portal; number of modules not stated.

reporting.notes: AOA-accredited (Category 1) sponsors report credits to the AOA; physicians self-report AMA PRA Category 1/AAFP credits with certificate, AOA ID and hours. CME Activity Report in AOA portal shows required totals.

aoaCme.cat1aMin: Set by each specialty board (no AOA-wide 1-A minimum stated for 2025-27); historical 30 Category 1-A minimum (unconfirmed for current cycle)
aoaCme.notes: Current cycle Jan 1, 2025 - Dec 31, 2027. 120 applies to non-time-limited DOs not in OCC; time-limited/OCC DOs meet their specialty board's number (AOBOO ophthalmology: 60 total, 25 specialty). Newly certified mid-cycle: prorated. Credits do not carry over between cycles. Category 1-B (e.g., osteopathic precepting) capped at 20% toward certification CME.

deaMate.appliesTo: All DEA-registered practitioners except those who are solely veterinarians (includes MDs, DOs, and optometrists holding DEA registrations)
deaMate.deadline: By the practitioner's next DEA registration submission (initial or renewal) on or after June 27, 2023; attested by a checkbox on the online form
deaMate.notes: Training on treating/managing patients with opioid or other substance use disorders. Hours may be cumulative across sessions/formats; training before Dec 29, 2022 and past DATA-waiver training count. Deemed compliant: board certification in addiction medicine/psychiatry, or graduation within 5 years of June 27, 2023 from a qualifying program with 8+ hours of curriculum. Accepted providers include ASAM, AAAP, AMA, AOA, ADA, APA, AAPA, ANCC and ACCME-accredited providers. COPE states COPE-accredited CE meets the requirement for ODs (course-by-course judgment). Attestation is not repeated at later renewals. Can also count toward ABO patient safety requirement.

creditTypes.amaCat1: AMA PRA Category 1 Credit: designated by ACCME (or state-recognized) accredited providers for certified activities, or directly by AMA for certain activities. Only physicians (MD, DO, or equivalent foreign degree) may be awarded it. Required type for ABO.
creditTypes.amaCat2: AMA PRA Category 2 Credit: self-designated and self-claimed by physicians for worthwhile, non-promotional learning not certified as Cat 1. No certificate issued; physician keeps own record (title, topic, dates, credits). 60 min = 1 credit, quarter-hour increments. Not accepted by some licensing/certifying bodies.
creditTypes.aoa: AOA assigns 4 categories: 1-A, 1-B, 2-A, 2-B. Category 1 = osteopathic CME; Category 2 = non-osteopathic CME. A = live activities; B = typically non-live (e.g., 1-B includes osteopathic precepting). AMA PRA Category 1 from ACCME providers is accepted as AOA Category 2 (2-A typically (unconfirmed)).
creditTypes.copeForMDs: Generally no: COPE-approved optometry CE is not AMA PRA Category 1 and does not satisfy ABO CME, which requires AMA PRA Category 1 from ACCME-accredited providers (unless the activity is also separately designated for AMA PRA Cat 1, e.g., by a jointly accredited provider).
creditTypes.amaForODs: Varies by state optometry board. Optometrists cannot be awarded AMA PRA Category 1 credit themselves (they usually receive a certificate of participation), but many boards accept CE from ACCME-accredited providers, sometimes with caps or topic limits; others require COPE-approved CE. Check each state board.
